headline: Apple Vision Pro M5 gets exclusive visionOS 27 features
summary: New visionOS 27 features are exclusive to the upcoming M5 model of the Apple Vision Pro, leaving original owners behind.
details: Apple's latest visionOS 27 update introduces two significant new capabilities for the Vision Pro headset.
However, these advanced features will be exclusive to the next-generation M5 model, meaning owners of the original Vision Pro will not be able to access them.
This move by Apple suggests a tiered approach to feature rollouts based on hardware capabilities, potentially disappointing early adopters of the Vision Pro.

The specific nature of these two exclusive features has not yet been detailed, but their exclusion from the original model highlights the potential for future hardware-dependent software advancements.

topic: norway restricts ai use for elementary school children
headline_marked: Norway [[bans AI tools for elementary school kids]]
headline: Norway bans AI tools for elementary school kids
summary: Norway imposes strict ban on generative AI tools for kids aged 6-13. The policy aims to focus education on reading, writing, and mathematics.
details: Norway is imposing a strict ban on the use of generative AI tools by elementary school kids, according to a report by Reuters. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere suggested at a press conference that AI lets children skip crucial steps in their education and that schools should focus on teaching them how to "read, write and do mathematics."

These standards will be imposed at the start of the new school year, which begins in late August. The ban impacts students from first through seventh grade, ages six to 13. However, the policy also extends to teens, albeit in a reduced fashion. Kids aged 14 to 16 can use generative AI, but only with a teacher's supervision.

Teens 17 and above are encouraged to use AI appropriately on their own. This isn't the first move Norway has made to remove tech from classrooms. The country banned smartphones from schools back in 2024, which has proven to be a success.

It led to a reduction in bullying, better grades and a significant decrease in the number of visits to psychologists for mental health issues. These results were especially potent with girls. Norway is also planning a social media ban for all children under 16, which is similar to how Australia handles things.
